newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Few Argentine state firms still up for grabs.
newsitem.headline: Few Argentine state firms still up for grabs.

text.p: Following the sale of a 30-year concession to run Argentina's state post office Encotesa Thursday, the country has few remaining major privatizations, as listed below:

* The state mortgage lender Banco Hipotecario Nacional, due to raise up to $3.0 billion. The sale was approved by Congress in July and windfalls have been earmarked for housing and infrastructure projects. No deadlines for the tender have been announced. The government is expected to seek up to $2.0 billion in bridge loan facilities on the strength of the sale to finance public works included in the 1997-1998 budgets.

* Thirty-six national airports, scheduled to be awarded in October in a single, 30-year concession which is expected to raise around $1.5 billion. The privatization was declared void in July by a judge who rejected the presidential decree authorizing it, but the government is appealing the ruling to the Supreme Court and says the sale will go ahead as planned.

* Hydroelectric plant Yacyreta. Argentina and Paraguay, joint owners, plan to call a tender for concessions to run the dam for an estimated $800 million. The Paraguayan Senate has approved the privatization, while in Argentina it is expected to be passed by decree, the same as the airport concession.

* The Atucha I and Embalse Rio Tercero nuclear power plants and the unfinished Atucha II. Congress gave approval in April to a law allowing their sale, expected to raise some $250 million. No tender deadlines have been announced.
The 30-year post office concession was won by the local Macri industrial group and Banco de Galicia, together with the British Post Office. They offered a $51.6 million six-monthly fee.
